name: bayesian_update_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Markets provide a stream of evidence (price movements, volume, spread changes) that can be used to update the probability of a stock trending up or down in the next 30 minutes via Bayesian updating. Starting with a prior based on NIFTY direction and sector strength, each 1-min bar's return, volume, and VWAP position provides likelihood evidence that updates the posterior probability. We trade when the posterior exceeds 0.70 (strong directional conviction). The inefficiency exists because Bayesian updating requires explicit probability modeling, which is foreign to most retail and many institutional intraday traders. The edge comes from formally aggregating heterogeneous evidence rather than relying on ad-hoc indicator combinations.
mechanism: Market microstructure varies across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes, mean-reversion dominates as market makers provide tight liquidity. In high-vol regimes, momentum persists as liquidity thins and stop-cascades amplify moves. Adapting the signal to the current regime captures the appropriate edge for prevailing conditions.

conditions: Posterior_Prob has been monotonically increasing for last 3 bars
Posterior_Prob has been monotonically decreasing for last 3 bars

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; recalibrate likelihood distributions if VIX > 20
filters.volume_filter: Volume_Likelihood must not be degenerate (volume > 100 shares per bar)

weaknesses: Likelihood distributions must be calibrated from historical data and are assumed stationary — market regime changes invalidate the calibration, requiring periodic recalibration (at least monthly)
Bayesian updating with multiple likelihoods assumes conditional independence between price, volume, and VWAP evidence, which is clearly violated (high volume and large price moves are correlated)
The prior based on NIFTY and sector direction introduces look-ahead if not carefully lagged; must use strictly prior-bar values to avoid data leakage
prior_art: Bayesian methods in finance: Johannes & Polson (2010); West & Harrison (1997) dynamic linear models; Bayesian portfolio allocation (Black-Litterman); application to intraday entry timing is less explored
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
